ideas.title: Putting over buried magnet stones
ideas.goal: A mini golf green in the dunes with magnet stones buried at random under it. You putt an iron ball and it bends, speeds up, stalls or gets caught by fields you can't see; before each putt you may sprinkle a little iron sand to read the break, like a golfer reads the slope. Fun because every green is new, you get better at reading the sand and aiming around a hidden pull, and friends play the same hole and miss in different ways.
ideas.toward: The ironsand project's goal (read the sand, find the stone) becomes a game you play again and again, and it is the first play loop where the field solver alone decides who wins; buried stones of any shape and pose work, nothing is placed per hole.
ideas.idea: The ball is a soft-iron sphere: in the buried stones' field (em.jl, any stone mesh and magnetisation) it carries the induced moment of a sphere of iron, m = 3V H (exact for a sphere, demagnetisation included), and the force is the gradient of m.B. It rolls as a rigid body with rolling resistance on sand and grass, the island's slope and the cup. The iron sand you sprinkle is physics/ironsand.jl's grains, so reading the green uses the same field the ball feels. A stone near the cup can hold a ball on the lip; two stones make a saddle the ball rides along.
ideas.form: A playable mini game in the human's game (aim with the beak, hold to set the strength, 9 to sprinkle), friends taking turns; a traced film of one putt curling round a hidden stone into the cup, with the sand pattern showing why.

ideas.title: The stone-and-ball cannon
ideas.goal: Lay a magnet stone in a wooden groove with iron balls on one side, roll one ball at it from the other, and the last ball leaves fast; stack stones and balls into stages to shoot further, at a tower of shells or a friend's bucket. Fun because the build decides the shot: how many stages, the gap, which face of the stone, and a wrong build just clacks.
ideas.toward: Fields really move parts: magnetic energy turned into motion through contacts, iron magnetising iron in the chain (soft iron solve), the materials table (iron answers, wood and shell don't).
ideas.idea: Stones as hard magnets (em.jl), balls as soft-iron spheres solved together with the stone, rigid-body contacts carrying the momentum through the chain (the impulse passes ball to ball), friction in the groove. The exit speed is what the field's energy gives, honest for a lodestone (a gentle shot, more stages more speed).
ideas.form: A bench toy in the human's game plus a short film of a three-stage shot knocking a shell tower down while Pickles ducks.
